references.text: Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh when he was swallowed by the great fish and vomited out again after three days. [ref:Jon 1:17|Jonas 1:17] refers to Jonah's time in the belly of the fish, which is the background for the sign Jesus mentions.

Jonah's preaching in Nineveh led the people to repent. [ref:Jon 3:4-5|Jonas 3:4-5] shows that Jonah himself became a sign to the Ninevites through his preaching and testimony, just as Jesus here compares himself with Jonah as a sign for his generation.

The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 12:40|Matteus 12:40] expands on the sign of Jonah by explaining that just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

In [ref:Matt 16:4|Matteus 16:4], Jesus repeats that this evil and adulterous generation will receive no other sign than the sign of Jonah, emphasizing that the death and resurrection of the Son of Man is the decisive sign for this generation.

The preceding verse [ref:Luk 11:29|Lukas 11:29] provides context: this generation is an evil generation that demands a sign, and the only sign it will receive is the sign of Jonah, which verse 30 explains further.
In [ref:Luk 11:32|Lukas 11:32], the comparison is expanded: the people of Nineveh repented at Jonah's preaching, but here there is something greater than Jonah – the Son of Man himself.

Jesus predicts his suffering, death, and resurrection on the third day in [ref:Luk 9:22|Lukas 9:22]. This is the fulfillment of the sign of Jonah: just as Jonah was restored from the abyss of death, so the Son of Man will rise from the dead.

In [ref:Joh 2:19-21|Johannes 2:19-21], Jesus speaks about tearing down the temple and raising it again in three days – a sign pointing to his death and resurrection, parallel to the sign of Jonah as the decisive sign of the Son of Man for this generation.
